preconditions.description: Attacker must control the admin wallet address (_adminWalletAddress) to receive reentrant calls
Contract must hold sufficient tokens to trigger swapAndLiquify (>= numTokensSellToAddToLiquidity)
swapAndLiquifyEnabled must be true to allow automatic swap execution

violation_target.exploit_hint: 1. Ensure attacker controls the _adminWalletAddress (set via _setReceiverWallet by owner). 2. Trigger token transfers to accumulate contract balance >= numTokensSellToAddToLiquidity. 3. Execute a transfer that triggers swapAndLiquify(). 4. During swapTokensForEth() external call to Uniswap router, the contract balance changes. 5. When sendBNBToAdmin() executes address(this).balance transfer to attacker-controlled admin wallet, reenter the contract before balance state is finalized. 6. Extract additional BNB through reentrant calls before the transfer completes.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has a reentrancy vulnerability in the sendBNBToAdmin() function. This function first calls swapTokensForEth() to swap tokens for ETH, then transfers address(this).balance to _adminWalletAddress. The vulnerability exists because: 1) The .transfer() call sends ALL contract balance to admin, 2) If attacker controls _adminWalletAddress, they receive the ETH, 3) During the transfer, attacker's receive() can reenter the contract. While inSwapAndLiquify modifier prevents recursive swapAndLiquify, the attacker can still call transfer() during reentrancy to collect fees or manipulate state. The key is that the admin wallet receives all ETH from the swap, and if attacker controls it, they profit directly.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate contract owner to set attacker as _adminWalletAddress via _setReceiverWallet(). 2. Inject tokens to attacker using deal(). 3. Transfer tokens to the contract to accumulate balance >= numTokensSellToAddToLiquidity threshold. 4. Execute a transfer that triggers swapAndLiquify(). 5. During sendBNBToAdmin(), ETH is transferred to attacker's address. 6. Attacker receives ETH profit from the swap.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get contract owner address via owner() view function. 2. vm.startPrank(owner) to impersonate owner. 3. Call _setReceiverWallet(payable(attacker)) to set attacker as admin. 4. vm.stopPrank(). 5. Use deal() to inject tokens to attacker. 6. Transfer tokens to contract to build up balance above threshold. 7. Execute final transfer to trigger swapAndLiquify. 8. Attacker receives ETH when sendBNBToAdmin transfers balance. 9. Assert attacker ETH balance increased.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The swapAndLiquify function calls swapTokensForEth which interacts with Uniswap router. For this to work, the pair needs ETH liquidity. Additionally, we need to ensure the contract has tokens above the threshold and all conditions are met for swapAndLiquify to trigger.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate owner to set attacker as admin wallet. 2. Inject ETH to the contract to provide liquidity for swaps. 3. Inject tokens to attacker. 4. Transfer tokens to contract to exceed threshold. 5. Trigger swapAndLiquify which will swap tokens for ETH and send to attacker. 6. Assert profit.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get owner and impersonate to set attacker as admin. 2. Deal ETH to contract for swap liquidity. 3. Deal tokens to attacker. 4. Transfer tokens to contract (must be from != uniswapV2Pair). 5. Trigger swapAndLiquify. 6. Verify attacker received ETH.
attempts.failure_reflection: The revert likely occurred because: 1) The Uniswap pair needs ETH liquidity for the swap to succeed, 2) We may need to provide initial ETH to enable the swap operation, 3) The transfer amounts or conditions might not be properly set up. The swapTokensForEth function requires the pair to have ETH reserves.

Transfer more tokens to contract to exceed threshold. 5. Trigger swapAndLiquify which will send ETH to attacker. 6. Assert profit.
